Score of candidate levels under their own cell weights (per-level detection)

Source: R/cellgloc_categorical.R
dot-gloc_cat_score.Rd

Under per-level detection (imputeCellGLoc(categorical = "em"), soft corner, since 7.5.1) every candidate \(k\) of a row \(i\) with a missing categorical cell – one level, or one level combination – carries its own cell weights \(W_k\), computed at its own design row \(u_k\). This function returns the score \(\ell_k\) by which the E-step judges such a candidate: the cellwise-penalised likelihood of the binary corner, with the candidate's posterior proportional to its prior times \(\exp(\ell_k)\).

.gloc_cat_score(
  X,
  M,
  Wc,
  B,
  Sigma,
  Ucand,
  row_of,
  w_min = 0.5,
  band = .gloc_peer_band
)

Arguments

X

\(n x p\) continuous matrix.

M

\(n x p\) missing mask.

Wc

cell weights, one row per candidate, in the order of Ucand.

B

\(q x p\) coefficients.

Sigma

\(p x p\) scatter.

Ucand

candidate design rows, one per candidate.

row_of

the data row of each candidate.

w_min, band

the peer rule.

Value

one score \(\ell_k\) per candidate.

Details

The score is

$$\ell_k = -\frac{1}{2} [ |K| \log 2\pi + \log\det G + y' G^{-1} y ] - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \in K} (1 - r_j) p_j - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{j \in O \setminus K} \lambda_j,$$

with \(O\) the observed continuous cells of row \(i\); \(r_j\) the peer reliability of cell \(j\) under \(W_k\) (.gloc_peer_rel, band included); \(K = \{j \in O : r_j > 0\}\); \(D = \mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{r_K})\) and \(G = D \Sigma_{KK} D + \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{jj} (1 - r_j))\) over \(K\), the noise-inflated construction of .gloc_cond_resid; \(y = \sqrt{r_K} \odot (x_{iK} - (B' u_k)_K)\); \(\lambda_j = \chi^2_{1;0.99} + \log 2\pi + \log c_j\) with \(c_j = 1 / (\Sigma^{-1})_{jj}\) (.gloc_lambda); and \(p_j = \lambda_j - \log(2\pi\sigma_{jj}) = \chi^2_{1;0.99} + \log(c_j / \sigma_{jj})\).

Endpoints. When every \(r_j\) is 0 or 1, \(\ell_k\) is exactly \(-1/2\) times row \(i\)'s term of the binary-corner objective (.gloc_objective) at the candidate's residuals \(x_i - B' u_k\) and weights, with \(\lambda\) from the same \(\Sigma\): the Gaussian log-density of the retained cells minus \(\lambda_j / 2\) per flagged observed cell. Missing cells are the same under every candidate and are left out, whatever their weight. Inside the band \(\ell_k\) is continuous in the weights: as \(r_j \to 0\), \(y_j \to 0\) and cell \(j\)'s row of \(G\) tends to \(\sigma_{jj}\), so the cell contributes \(-\frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi\sigma_{jj})\), and \(p_j\) tops that up to \(\lambda_j / 2\). The E-step therefore stays continuous in \(W\), which the fixed-point argument of the peer band needs. When every candidate of a row carries the row's weight row, \(\ell_k\) differs from .gloc_cat_loglik by one constant within the row, wherever the Cholesky factorisation of \(G\) succeeds; on a \(G\) that is not positive definite the two fall back differently (MASS::ginv there, the eigenvalue floor here).

Why. A cell that fits candidate \(c\) is retained under \(c\) and flagged under a candidate it does not fit, so \(c\) gains up to \(\chi^2_{1;0.99} / 2 \approx 3.3\) log units from it. With one weight row per observation, computed at the expected design row, the cell that decides the level was flagged under every candidate and dropped from all of them, and the posterior could not move (the flag lock of 7.5.0). A cell that fits no candidate is flagged under every candidate, pays the same penalty under each and leaves the density under each, so its effect on the level is that of a missing cell.

\(\Sigma\) is the scatter of the current iteration (Ruling R71), so the density and the penalty sit on one scale. If .gloc_lambda(Sigma) gives no penalty, \(c_j = \sigma_{jj}\), with a warning. \(\log\det G\) and \(G^{-1}\) come from the Cholesky factor of \(G\); if that fails, from its eigenvalues floored at 1e-8 times the largest, the floor of .gloc_psd. Candidates whose reliabilities are all 0 or 1 share one factorisation per pattern; a candidate with a cell inside the band gets its own.
